pr_body:
This PR replaces #5963 (which contains a lot of discussion on the redis<->systemd interaction) and fixes #5826.

I hope it's OK to take this easy way out of the mess I somehow managed to created in my old PR.
pr_comments: @jtru my condolences and may his soul rest in peace.
@jtru I'm sorry to hear such sad news :-( my condolences.

@jtru P.S. I bet you already understood the mood here, but we consider OSS contribution to the Redis project as a huge gift, and there are no time windows to reply, get work done, it could take 3 years and we are ok :-D No rush in general is our motto.

Thank you both for your very kind and uplifting words. The Redis community really is special because of people like you.

I tried to implement @ulidtko's suggestions (thanks again for your feedback!), except for the copyright license notice in the example unit files — if @antirez feels it's really warranted to have even more boiler-plate in this rather dull artifact, he may add it, of course.

Hey @jtru, hope you're well!

I've been told there's another systemd feature: [EXTEND_TIMEOUT_USEC][*]. Redis could call `sd_notifyf(0, "EXTEND_TIMEOUT_USEC=%n", _extend_usec);` to ask systemd to **extend the start timeout**. Also described in [man systemd.service][man]. This would perfectly solve your older compatibility concern (from #5963) with zero user-side configuration.

Having said that, this PR ✔ Looks Good To Me as it stands, I'd approve merging.

[man]: https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/systemd.service.html
[*]: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/99b43caf26787ac9376e10c14f6a5bcf056f900c/man/sd_notify.xml#L198

Thank you, I'm doing better these days :)

I am aware of the timeout extension mechanism, and I agree that it'd be the best way to handle this scenario - but I'm not familiar enough with the Redis codebase (yet? :)) to be able to come up with an actual implementation proposal/patch that preempts the database loading/replica sync process to pester systemd with liveliness updates.

@antirez: Apart from additional reviewers' approval, is there anything you'd like to have added/changed for being able to merge this PR?

I'd like to try getting the timeout extension mechanism during shutdown implemented in another PR, if you're interested, because I'm not sure how quickly I can find enough time to work on it.

Ok, let me suggest these actions.

 1. Edit this PR to say it "fixes #5826", not "re-does #5963".
 2. Close #5963 referring people to #6052 (this PR), to shut down any further confusion.
 3. Determine whether we do EXTEND_TIMEOUT_USEC in this PR, or later in a separate future PR.
 4. Resolve the ABI issues with `dlopen("libsystemd.so")` raised by @guillemj in #5963.

-----

My own opinion on point 3: only a very slight preference to "do it later". Whichever way works fine for me.

-----

On point 4: @guillemj raises valid concerns. However, I don't like a lot the proposed solution ("some kind of redis plugin...") for the extra complexity which it entails.

Instead, how about we just **revert** `redisCommunicateSystemd` to the raw `socket(AF_UNIX, SOCK_DGRAM)` approach, effectively **reimplementing sd_notify()**, as it was before?.. This has a number of advantages.
 * No `dlopen("libsystemd.so")`, no `-lsystemd` neither, no any plugins. No curses from packagers and distro maintainers.
 * Why pull a [tricky, dynamically-optional] dependency when we only need one function from it?..
 * Frankly, the `sd_notify()` function is not the easiest to (re)implement! I've tried that before, and failed. Apparently, the original author of `redisCommunicateSystemd()`, @pyr, didn't fail in reimplementing `sd_notify()` (however did indeed a sloppy job overall, as #5826 states; but blaming is not to the point). What I'm trying to say is having more implementations of `sd_notify()` besides the [libsystemd one][•], especially simplified & self-contained, could be beneficial.
 * Finally: this approach is miles easier to follow. It's simple and neat comparing with *redis plugins*.

Disadvantages of the same:
 * This is a form of code duplication. It has a price; balancing that VS the "unlinking" from libsystemd.so is not trivial.
 * Redis might want to integrate with more libsystemd goodies in the future. Socket activation. This will become harder and harder to manage without `libsystemd.so`.

Turning systemd support in Redis into a compile-time toggle is another option. I don't like it a lot, too.

@guillemj, can we just seal this DLL can'o'worms with simply `dlopen("libsystemd.so.0")` ?

[•]: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/21042737f0686bc27dc620da53d11de072579924/src/libsystemd/sd-daemon/sd-daemon.c#L562

Thank you, everyone, for your feedback! I'll try to address the points made that are related to the C components this patch affects below.

@guillemj: Thanks a lot for spotting that soname mistake; I wasn't acitvely aware of that peculiarity, since my primary development machine runs a distro that doesn't even have -dev packages, and libsystemd.so is always there. I'll make sure to also test my builds/changes on Debian, too, to remedy that.

I'd actually have preferred to just link to libsystemd at compile-time myself, but I wouldn't know how to do so gracefully with redis' beautifully simple build system. If there's a way to do that, that'd be a vastly better solution than the approach I chose - please let me know if I missed it.

Now if/when systemd decides to require a soname bump for libsystemd, I don't think it'd be warranted or wise to assume that the notification interface for service readiness will continue to work the exact same way it did with the .0 version - so I don't think that re-implementing `sd_notify()` inline/ad-hoc is the *proper* solution to the problem exposed, either.

I'm not familiar with redis plugins/modules yet, so I don't know if implementing the notify feature as such a thing could effectively side-step the problem. I'm pretty sure you want systemd notification support to be core feature of the server, and if that redis plugin/module was shipped and built with redis proper, I think you'd end up in the same situation as with modifying redis-server itself: You either `dlopen()` a hard-coded soname version, or you modify the build system to figure out the proper filename by itself. At which point you could just modify the compiler flags during building and conditionally include header files to link libsystemd at compile time, which leads us up a few paragraphs in my ramblings :)

Offloading the talking-to-systemd part to an external utility that redis would `execve` after forking has at least two problems of its own, I think: On Linux, `clone()`ing a process that has lots of memory allocated (like many redis instances we run at work have), due to the CoW semantics involved, that's not guaranteed to succeed (and sure as hell not guaranteed to do so in a timely manner :)). The other (potential; I haven't verified that empirically) problem is that systemd will only accept readiness protocol messages from the unit's MAINPID, which by default is the first process the service spawned. One can change that property at runtime, but it involves using, yeah you guessed right, `sd_notify()`... so that's kinda catch-22 for our hypothetical child process helper, which should be the only thing that's able to use `sd_notify()`, but that the service manager won't listen to.

I'm not sure where to go from here. Will have to think about it some more; all your comments and guidance are _highly_ appreciated!

@jtru Hey, no problem!

Making libsystemd optional at compile-time is probably the most straight forward option, and something that I think most distributions would be fine with. The majority will just leave it enabled by default, and the few that have systemd allergy can disable it if they want. Sorry for not explicitly mentioning this, as I thought the run-time selection was desirable for some reason. To hook that up I think you'd just need to add a new `USE_LIBSYSTEMD`, and then based on that in `src/Makefile` add the output of `$(shell pkg-config --libs libsystemd)` to `FINAL_LIBS` and the output of `$(shell pkg-config --cflags libsystemd)` to `FINAL_CFLAGS`. You probably want to use `PKG_CONFIG ?= pkg-config`, and then use that make variable instead of a bare pkg-config, so that cross-building works (when cross-building the tool would be usually called stuff like _gnu-triplet_-pkg-config, like with the compiler).

Now, I'd still like to clarify some things about the dlopen() issue and the other possible solutions, even if the above makes it irrelevant.

Re the SONAME getting bumped, I'd expect the notification protocol to still be compatible, as stated in https://www.freedesktop.org/wiki/Software/systemd/InterfaceStabilityPromise/. It might just mean any of the types or function signatures in the library or the sd_notify(3) C interface might have changed (which might affect a solution based on libsystemd, but not one on a custom protocol implementation).

Re the plugin, I don't think redis has any plugin framework, and that might not even be desired. The way this would work here is that redis would build something like a `redis-systemd.so` plugin, that would link at build time against `libsystemd.so` (which would point at whatever is the current SONAME), so in most cases a simple rebuild even after a SONAME bump would just work, or the compiler would error out due to type issues or missing symbols. Then redis itself would `dlopen("redis-systemd.so")` and that would always be guaranteed to work, because both have been compiled with the same set of options, and share the same internal API/ABI. Of course if the sd_notify(3) C interface has changed, then that would require code changes, but that would be the case for any libsystemd solution anyway, the difference is that with proper build-time dynamic linking, most of the work and checks gets done for free. When it comes to distributions, some could decide to either not build the plugin at all, or ship it in another different package for example, so that installing redis-server would not pull the libsystemd dependency. But this all seems like an overcomplex solution just to avoid the dependency, I think the compile-time option should be good enough for everyone, really.

Re the executable notifier, the memory usage should really not be a problem, as Linux uses by default overcommit, and the child will not be touching the memory, so the only thing it has is the same page tables, and the fork() would be followed by an immediate execve() anyway, but if this is considered to be a potential problem there's always the option of using posix_spawn() or vfork(); for the readiness protocol access, the service file could always set NotifyAccess=all.

Hope that clarifies everything! :)

Good! So we do settle on `WITH_SYSTEMD` compile-time toggle, am I right?

There's still the other option of a helper executable, it will definitely work with `NotifyAccess=all`. But IMO, an `#ifdef WITH_SYSTEMD` is much preferred.
I will try to get a patch implemented that, if available, links `libsystemd` at build-time tomorrow.

I just pushed a change that makes the build system link `libsystemd` if redis is being built on Linux, and `pkg-config` provides information about `libsystemd`. @guillemj I'd be very grateful if you could review that iteration of my PR, too :)


I am still convinced this is an improvement over the original implementation of the `supervised systemd` configuration, but I start to have my doubts about that particular configuration option (and its supported values) itself: Upstart is dead upstream (and not used by and maintained distro - both afaik), so supporting it is an effort of questionable utility. To be able to manually configure supervision to actually mismatch the provided environment seems like a rather powerful footgun, and that possibility (together with the current behaviour of "trying to make the best out of all possible combinations of configuration and perceived reality") leaves the server process between a rock and a hard place: Should it quit on its own and scream about the probable configuration error, or should it just try to soldier on, under the looming threat of the service manager shooting it down violently after 'TimeoutStartSec' have exceeded?

My most recent patch implements `USE_SYSTEMD` as I think/hope you suggested it.

I believe it would be worthwhile if the build-process itself reported what course of action in regard to linking `libsystemd` was chosen (either by the user, or automatically), but since there's no common infrastructure for communicating such information to the user (like `QUIET_CC`, `QUIET_LINK` etc. provide for wrapping various build-time output), I didn't implement anything like that right now. So, for `USE_SYSTEMD=auto` builds, one would have to check the compiled executables for having libsystemd registered in their ELF dynamic section to know which way was taken.


I fully agree that maybe removing `supervised auto` (and possibly also `upstart`) from the range of valid configuration options should be discussed in another ticket or PR.

@jtru Hey, I'm not actually sure what's the policy within redis about MR and commits, but personally it would help with reviewing if you could apply some «git rebase -i» on the series and fold any patch so that the end result is a set of atomic and logical changes, that do not flip-flop the implementations? :)

I don't know if @antirez has some sort of policy in place for this (I haven't found one in the very friendly "how to contribute"-parts of the docs), but yeah, I'll try to come up with a cleaner history for this PR/branch today in the evening! (I hope that a force-push won't interfere with GitHub's web-based magic while I am at that, but I guess I will have to find out the hard way ;))

@guillemj, I hope you find this history easier to digest. I chose not to erase the original approach of using `dlopen()` from it, because discussing the pros and cons and actually implementing it was a valuable learning experience for me. If upstream prefers an even cleaner history, I can still deliver that with another rebase - it's @antirez's call :)

Thanks! I'd still rearrange the commits so that the first one switches the internal implementation to use libsystemd (with no interim dlopen switch), and then another that adds the new improved notifications to systemd. :)

I'd say, git history doesn't *need* to be absolutely perfect; although it's certainly great when it is.

Just consider that the previous *implementation* was far from perfect, let alone its history. Implementation is what matters the most.

That is to say, I feel @jtru has applied substantial effort already; and the current commit history is *fine*. 

Thus, we'd bring this PR to a `[Ready To Merge]` title tag, wouldn't we?

I don't mean to rush anything, git exercise is always useful to do, however at least aiming to wrap this up and finally merge is clearly in everyone's best interest. Distributions will take a looong time to ship this, remember?..

I'd very much like to have @antirez decide what history for this PR should look like :) I'm very open to make any sensible changes requested (but I feel unable to decide which way/variant makes the most sense).

I would also like to work on other "supervision"-related improvements after this initial effort has met the bar to get merged.
@antirez, are you still considering merging this feature? Please let me know what you'd need me do to help you decide - thanks! :)
*ping* :)

> _ping_ :)

Hey @antirez, are you willing to merge this at all?

Months go by, you've released 5.0.6 without this PR (i.e. with broken systemd support), and we've got file conflicts again. All this despite a thorough review by 4 people.

Is there anything blocking your decision to merge? Can we help?
Hello all, I'm ready to merge, please rebase and ping me. Sorry for the delay. Putting this into the Redis 6 milestone.
Ping @jtru @ulidtko

Hey, I'd be glad to rebase, however it's a branch/fork of @jtru and I [won't be able][•] to push there anyway... So we'd wait until he does it.

[•]: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/22237609/adding-to-someone-else-s-pull-request-on-a-github-project-that-i-do-not-own

In fact, no big deal -- a pretty obvious code move happened, single conflict taken 10 minutes to resolve.

https://github.com/ulidtko/redis/tree/better-systemd-integration-v2.rebased -- pushed here.

Thanks for reconsidering this feature, @antirez - and thanks for figuring out the resolution to the merge conflict, @ulidtko :)

Salvatore, can you/do you want to pull from Maxim's fork, or shall I redo the rebase on mine? (Still unfamiliar with Github's common workflows, I'm not sure what's more common or convenient.)

Awesome! No problem I can merge from there as well. However a few questions.

* I saw ` /* XXX TODO is this sufficient to pass readiness control off to readSyncBulkPayload()? */
` inside the code. Is this issue fixed now and we can drop the comment?
* Do I understand correctly that the default is don't even try to auto detect if there is the systemd library installed?

Thanks

Let me answer the latter: yes at build time, no at runtime. Build-time `libsystemd` detection is in the Makefile, overridable with `USE_SYSTEMD` (both ways, force on, force off). The runtime detection is in `redisIsSupervised()` and just checks the environment variable `NOTIFY_SOCKET` which systemd sets. Then if set, `redisCommunicateSystemd()` calls the library's `sd_notify` API directly, if not build-disabled.

So, if we have redis compiled with USE_SYSTEMD and there's no libsystemd at runtime — the binary won't run, with `error while loading shared libraries: libsystemd.so.0` from ld.so. Which is pretty normal, even expected failure mode I'd say.

redis with USE_SYSTEMD but absent NOTIFY_SOCKET environment will load the `libsystemd.so.0` library, but *won't use it* — so you can pass any empty `libsystemd.so`-looking stub, and run anyway in those awkward situations. Those shouldn't normally happen though.

Distro maintainers, I believe, are okay with such setup — and not so okay with alternatives involving `dlopen()`. We've discussed this above extensively, and arrived at the current version.

-----

Regarding the TODO: I can't quite... Ah! I get it. Yes it is sufficient; remove the comment. In standalone mode, we say `READY=1` at the comment point; however in replicated mode, we delay sending `READY=1` until the replication sync completes.

Thanks to @ulidtko's helping hand, I had much less of a hassle performing the deed than I had expected. (We do use git at work, but not a workflow involing pull requests - it's always a bit of a mind-bending exercise to me to interact with a GitHub-hosted project, I have to admit.)

I hope things are clear to merge this way, @antirez. Please let us know if anything's still holding you back! :)
Thank you, PR merged.

issue_context.title: Systemd readiness signalling is implemented incorrectly
issue_context.body:
Hi!

We're using Redis 5.0.3 with `supervised systemd`. We also set systemd `Type=notify` for Redis units, since many of our application services declare ordering dependencies like `After=redis@foo.service`, `After=redis@bar.service`.

We want to *absolutely eliminate* any races during parallel service startup, to *never ever* allow failures like this to happen:

```
  [...]
  File "/usr/lib/python2.7/site-packages/redis/client.py", line 640, in flushall
    return self.execute_command('FLUSHALL')
  File "/usr/lib/python2.7/site-packages/redis/client.py", line 571, in execute_command
    return self.parse_response(connection, command_name, **options)
  File "/usr/lib/python2.7/site-packages/redis/client.py", line 577, in parse_response
    response = connection.read_response()
  File "/usr/lib/python2.7/site-packages/redis/connection.py", line 569, in read_response
    response = self._parser.read_response()
  File "/usr/lib/python2.7/site-packages/redis/connection.py", line 241, in read_response
    raise error
BusyLoadingError: Redis is loading the dataset in memory
```

In this case, an application service with `After=redis@foo.service` has had politely waited for Redis startup (through systemd mediation), and then tried connecting to the said Redis to do its own stuff. Circumstantially, Redis was not ready for service at this time — **despite having reported READY=1**.

Consulting the source, I can easily see that **redis lies to systemd** about its readiness:
https://github.com/antirez/redis/blob/b4867130f40e2df366b740e118405187608856ae/src/server.c#L4156-L4197

There's a big pile of stuff happening between `READY=1` gets sent in `redisIsSupervised()`, and when the server is actually ready *for real*.

-----

I'm open to discussion on what anyone wants to define as "ready for real" — but the main point remains: `sd_notify(READY=1)` is a crucial feature in reliability contexts, and Redis implements it wrong.
comments:
We've been bitten by this behaviour myself, and I think the existing behaviour could be improved drastically. Afaics, there's three cases to cover:

1. standalone `redis-server` with no persistence configured, or no persistence artifacts to load
2. `redis-server` as primary/master or standalone with AOF or RDB state to pick up
3. `redis-server` as secondary/slave

The easiest case is scenario 1, which is what the current behaviour (fully or only partially? I'm not 100% sure) covers - just tell the service manager it's good to go once the server is able to accept reads and writes.

The other two cases should delay signalling readiness until the dataset has been completely loaded from its source. I'm not familiar enough with the codebase yet to be able to tell there's a common synchronisation point for this, but for the replication case, the bottom of [src/replication.c:readSyncBulkPayload](https://github.com/antirez/redis/blob/unstable/src/replication.c#L1318) could be the place for the magic to happen.

A way to implement this, I think, would be to have [src/server.c:redisSupervisedSystemd](https://github.com/antirez/redis/blob/unstable/src/server.c#L4626) take an argument to pass on into systemd's notification socket (and rework the function so that you can call it more than once during the lifetime of the `redis-server` process), change the current location where "READY=1" is being signalled to tell systemd something like "STATUS=Redis is loading the dataset into memory..." instead, and have the aforementioned condition for the loading having finished cause emitting a truthful "READY=1".


While we are at that, one might want to (conditionally) include `systemd/sd-daemon.h` and use `sd_notify()` instead of handling this internally/manually - but I'm not sure how @antirez feels about that kind of change/added dependency, and how it would fit with redis' current (lack of a configurable - which doesn't mean I don't like it! :)) build system.


Furthermore, I'm actually pretty sure that implementing this will not completely isolate your clients from having to deal with the "Redis is loading..."-condition - at least not when you're daeling with a replica that decides it has to do a full resync due to having lost track of the primary (since depdendent services will already have been started by systemd in that case, and you cannot seem to transition a systemd service from "READY=1" to a non-ready state). But even so, it would make life for us a _lot_ easier if the initial "READY=1" message were closer to the (momentary) truth.
I started working on this; if you're interested, please have a look at https://github.com/jtru/redis/tree/better-systemd-integration

review_comments:
From your comment in the PR, I think I have to agree that the option does not seem to make much sense anymore? I'd personally just call this function unconditionally, and deprecate the config option. If the caller, be that systemd or start-stop-daemon, sets the `NOTIFY_SOCKET` environment variable, then `sd_notify()` will send the notification, otherwise not. This looks like the most common behavior used everywhere else.

But perhaps that should be in another commit, if the change is desired.
